causal.selection: Seven previously accepted failures; not a prevalence sample

saved_integrity_report.scan_limitation: Known credential formats only; not a general sensitivity classifier

scope: Read-only reaggregation of frozen saved evidence; no new outcomes, API calls, replay or test run

source_limitations: Exploratory follow-up was designed after the core comparison; it is not confirmatory or a replacement for core results.
Common authorship and developer knowledge intentionally align valid semantic cases with anticipated unsupported assumptions.
Concrete mutation recipes are new but broad defect categories overlap the core taxonomy.
The semantic-relation stratum is an exploratory transfer diagnostic, not a blinded held-out population.
Engineered mutants are not natural model errors; a favorable result would not establish directed testing as generally best.
Fresh random seeds are independent of validation seeds; parameterized semantic finals reuse example structures and can exactly repeat empty cases.
Semantic cases are much smaller than ordinary generated inputs; equal test count does not imply equal logical work or input diversity.
Every mutant, including inapplicable or untriggered recipes, remains in the all-mutant denominator.
The observed-counterexample denominator is conditional on this finite corpus and is not an equivalence proof.
Native oracle cost is not isolated in logical counters; observed wall time includes setup and is machine dependent.
The sixteen related templates and repeated mutants do not constitute independent inferential samples.
No formal API candidate was inspected, no API calls were made, and effect correctness is outside this computational supplement.

source_limitations: Authored deterministic mutants are not a representative sample of natural model errors.
Held-out labels denote a prespecified diagnostic partition; one benchmark team authored all operators and tests.
Primitive targeted transforms are generic, but engineered fault prevalence controls strategy rankings.
The final transform holdout uses unseen compositions of seen primitives, not unseen primitive transformations.
No counterexample observed does not establish semantic equivalence; identity and untriggered mutants remain in all-mutant denominators.
Empirically non-equivalent denominators are conditional on observing a semantic counterexample anywhere in this fixed finite corpus.
Correct controls are sixteen benchmark solvers, not all possible correct programs.
The four targeted tests share one seed; the other strategies use four seeds.
Logical cost counts bounded-interpreter work, not wall time, host-side oracle work, or API cost.
Stopping on resource bounds is reported separately and does not prove a semantic defect.
Cases, mutants and templates are related; per-mutant counts are descriptive, not independent inferential samples.
This computational study does not test effect correctness or safety; those are separate v15 campaigns.
